title: The Silence Where You Can Hear
description: Eight steps of attention practice: honest about benefit and risk, with a companion between sessions and a living circle at the end

units.title: The agreement: what is here and what is not
Breath: the anchor you always carry
Body: a scan with your eyes open
The uncomfortable: what to do when it surfaces
Talking with AI: an interlocutor, not a curator
The circle: where all of this leads

objectives.text: State what the course does not do: it does not treat, does not replace therapy, does not work with trauma
Choose the duration and intensity of practice within the course ceiling and explain why “more” does not mean “better” here
Recognize a stop signal and pick an action: stop and return, or, when thoughts of self-harm arise — crisis line or a professional
Distinguish what the AI companion does from what it should not do
Explain why the course leads to living people and a circle, and state what the circle does not do

checks.question: How does the course define its place relative to therapy?
options: The course does not treat and does not replace therapy; at best it sits beside a specialist
The course can replace therapy while you wait for a specialist appointment
The course works gently with trauma if you go slowly
The course replaces therapy for those without a diagnosis
checks.explain: In the first step the course states outright that it does not treat, does not replace therapy, and does not work with trauma: clinical context is required for that (u1, “What the course does not do”).

checks.question: What duration limits does the course set?
options: Start with 10 minutes and reach an hour by week 8
Duration doesn’t matter if you practice without missing a hundred days in a row
As long as there’s no discomfort
Usually 10–20 minutes, ceiling — 30–45 minutes per session, no home retreats and no “hundred days straight”
checks.explain: There is no evidence that “more” equals “better”, and intensity and retreats are listed as risk factors. Therefore the course sets a ceiling (u2, “‘More’ does not mean ‘better’”).

checks.question: During a scan a certain area feels uncomfortable. What does the course suggest?
options: Stay in that area a bit longer to finish the pass
Leave the area immediately, return your gaze to an external object; if it intensifies, stand up and walk
Close your eyes to focus better on the sensation
“Breathe into the tension” to release it
checks.explain: The task is to stay inside the window of tolerance, not to finish the scan. Eyes stay open, an external return point and the right to stop are standard course elements. “Breathing into pain” belongs to therapy language, not the course (u3).

checks.question: While naming, excitement arises: “I’ll note everything, nothing will be missed.” How does the course interpret this?
options: As a sign of progress: attention sharpens
As a reason to extend the session until the excitement passes
As a signal to slow down and return to clean breathing for a minute
As a cue to move to intensive noting
checks.explain: Naming in the course is a light ten-minute annotation. Continuous intense noting without a teacher is not given to beginners: it’s a “speed-up” practice (u4, “The line that must not be crossed here”).

checks.question: Which of these does the course label a stop signal that requires ending the session?
options: A sense of unreality of self or world that does not pass after practice
Attention repeatedly drifts into thoughts
In one body area you “don’t feel” anything
The session was boring
checks.explain: Wandering mind and “don’t feel” are considered normal parts of the exercise (u2, u3). The unreality feeling is listed among stop signals in step 5.

checks.question: During the course thoughts of self-harm appear. What does the course say?
options: Shorten sessions to five minutes and keep going
Exit the learning scenario immediately and reach a living person: a professional or a crisis line (in the US — 988, other countries — findahelpline.com)
Discuss it with the AI companion: that’s what it’s for
Wait for the circle meeting and share there
checks.explain: This stop signal is not a cue to reduce dosage, but a cue to seek a living person right away. Neither the course text, nor the companion, nor the circle chat serve as crisis help (u5, u7, u8).

checks.question: How should the course be understood when a difficult experience surfaces in practice?
options: It means you’re practicing incorrectly
It means you’ve progressed and should endure it
It means the practice isn’t suitable for you at all
It means the dose is currently high and should be reduced
checks.explain: The interpretation changes how long the difficulty lasts. Therefore the course does not call it an error or progress: it’s a signal to lower the dose (u5, “The words you explain difficulty to yourself with are an intervention”).

checks.question: Which of these requests should the AI companion not fulfill?
options: Suggest practicing longer because everything is going well
Parse session notes one question at a time
Remind why the course has a duration ceiling
Help craft two-three phrases for living people
checks.explain: Session unpacking, material repetition, and phrase preparation for the circle are within the companion’s role. Pushing for longer duration or intensity is on the “blocklist” (u7).

checks.question: Why does this course place AI between sessions rather than instead of people?
options: The model still answers meditation questions worse than a human
Living people are needed only for crisis cases
Research shows that digital programs work better with a human in the loop
It’s cheaper for the course
checks.explain: A guided format yields a noticeably larger effect than solo work, even when the guide isn’t a clinician. Hence AI fills the gap between lessons, and the course leads to living people (u7, u8).

checks.question: A circle participant brings up more than fits in one evening. What should the circle do according to the course rules?
options: Discuss his experience with the whole circle to give feedback
Suggest he practice longer to work through it
Ask him to tell everything to the end since he’s already started
Not interpret or treat, but help him get to a specialist
checks.explain: The circle is not a therapy group: they do not interpret others’ experience or treat each other. Its task is to help the person reach a specialist. Additionally, each person has the right to stay silent or leave (u8, “How to assemble a circle that stands a chance”).
